hook: Follow a talk on sleep from claim to advice, knowing where each answer will turn up before you hear it.
intro: A lecture on sleep of about 280 words, heard once, in the order almost every lecture follows: a greeting and a claim (Viele von uns schlafen zu wenig), evidence (Studien zeigen, dass Erwachsene durchschnittlich sieben bis acht Stunden brauchen), a consequence (Wer dauerhaft weniger schläft, riskiert gesundheitliche Probleme), a second factor (Neben der Dauer ist aber auch die Qualität des Schlafes entscheidend), a cause (das blaue Licht der Bildschirme), and a recommendation in the Konjunktiv (Weniger Bildschirmzeit am Abend würde vielen Menschen besseren Schlaf bringen). Lectures, podcasts and radio features are built like this, and the questions follow the talk in order; the skill is recognising the lecture’s moves so the answers arrive where you expect them. Numbers (sechs, sieben bis acht) and qualifiers (nur zum Teil, eher kühl) are the usual traps, and the recommendation is nearly always the last question.
tips[0].title: The lecture's moves
tips[0].text: Greeting + claim (Viele von uns schlafen zu wenig) → evidence (Studien zeigen, dass …) → consequence (Wer …, riskiert …) → second factor (Neben der Dauer ist … entscheidend) → cause (blaues Licht) → recommendation (würde … bringen). Map the seven questions onto them.
tips[0].check.why: Studien zeigen, dass … is the classic signal that the speaker is backing up the claim with evidence.
tips[0].visual.moves[0].label: Claim
tips[0].visual.moves[1].label: Evidence
tips[0].visual.moves[2].label: Explanation
tips[0].visual.moves[3].label: Advice
tips[1].title: wer …, (der) … = anyone who
tips[1].text: Wer dauerhaft weniger schläft, riskiert gesundheitliche Probleme. The wer-clause is a generalising relative — the subject of the main clause. Consequence questions point to it.
tips[1].check.why: wer … opens a generalising clause: anyone who does this. It is the subject of schläft schlechter.
tips[2].title: The recommendation is in the Konjunktiv
tips[2].text: würde … bringen, wäre … besser, könnte … helfen — when the speaker switches to würde / wäre / könnte, the advice has begun.
tips[2].check.why: The switch to the Konjunktiv (wäre) marks the recommendation; the others are claim and evidence.
remember[0]: Claim – evidence – consequence – factor – cause – recommendation.
remember[1]: Numbers, qualifiers (nur zum Teil) and the würde-sentence are the targets.
exam: Lectures and radio features like this are a standard listening text in the B2 exam — and the way you meet science in podcasts and on the radio.
tips[1].check.q: ‘Wer abends viel Kaffee trinkt, schläft schlechter.’ Who sleeps worse?
tips[1].check.options[0]: Anyone who drinks a lot of coffee in the evening
tips[1].check.answer: Anyone who drinks a lot of coffee in the evening
